messages:
maria: FYI canary just hit multiple OOMs after the prefetch/backpressure change merged earlier today. saw it on 4 nodes in eu-west-1, memory jumped ~30% within 10m.

josh: ugh, which PR? i remember the prefetch window tweak (#4923) and the backpressure patch (#4931) were landed together.

maria: right — #4931 enabled aggressive prefetch when backlog < 8, and #4923 changed default prefetch lookahead to 512.

sophia: logs? stack traces? heap profiles?

maria: attaching quick snippets — stack traces show slab allocs from kv_spill_path and lots of small arena growth.

maria: ```
OOM: runtime: out of memory
goroutine 1 [running]:
/runtime.mallocgc(...)
redwood/serving/kv.(*Cache).prefetch(...)
redwood/serving/kernel.SelectKernel(...)
```

josh: that stack points to prefetch triggering kernel selection hotpath — maybe it allocs temp buffers during lookahead.

oliver: CI also had a perf reg fail on the same commit: perf/latency median +18% on longctx tests. not huge but correlated. job 5482.

max: i ran a heap profile diff on a repro worker. big spike in small objects pinned to slab buckets when sequence_len > 2048. prefetch ramped up and caused cache churn + fragmentation.

sophia: how deterministic? can we bisect to a single commit?

maria: bisecting now — testing rollback of #4931 (backpressure change) first. will report.

ci-bot: perf job 5482 failed: latency_regression (p = 0.02). See https://ci.redwood.ai/job/5482

josh: if the backpressure change removes throttling, prefetch could overwhelm KV cache and force evictions mid-request, causing allocation storms. that fits memory and latency.

maria: bisect update: rolled back #4931 on canary -> immediate reduction in mem growth, no OOMs in 45m. reapplying #4923 (prefetch window=512) alone seems ok.

sophia: so the backpressure logic likely the culprit. maybe it drops backpressure signals too early and prefetch runs unbounded when backlog flaps.

oliver: kernel selection comment: we also changed fast-path kernel priority in same release (kernel-router change), which reduced kernel fallback but increased temp buffer reuse. could be interacting.

max: i captured `pprof` before/after revert. attach hashes: before: a1f3c, after: b2d9e. diff shows 70% of new allocs from `kv.prefetcher.fetchSegment` and `kv.slab.allocateSmall`

maria: decision: hold rollout for the release, reverted #4931 from canary, flagging as rollout-blocker.

deploy-bot: Rollout halted for release r-2026-03-18 due to healthchecks (OOMs).

josh: next steps: 1) write unit test for backpressure saturation case 2) add a cap to prefetch inflight (e.g., max 4) 3) add metrics for prefetch-inflight and kv-evict-rate per-seq-len bucket 4) check kernel-router fast-path interactions.

sophia: i'll own the test and the metric. can someone add the cap as a short fix? if it reduces memory, we can re-run canary.

maria: tagging @enginfrastructure for infra-level OOM tracking and @sre to check alerting.

oliver: also note: long sequence lengths (>2048) now disproportionately trigger prefetch; maybe the heuristic should be seq_len-aware (reduce lookahead for longctx).

max: i'll prototype an inflight cap + seq_len-based backoff and run against the longctx perf harness. if it stabilizes, we can land a targeted fix instead of full revert.

maria: thanks. logging action items in the release ticket. for immediate safety we keep revert in canary and mark rollout blocked.

ci-bot: bisect result: culprit narrowed to commit 6f7d2c3 (backpressure: drop prefetch if backlog < 8).

josh: note for postmortem: include pprof diffs, CI perf graphs, and how kernel selection changes amplified the effect.

maria: ok folks, let's sync in 30m in #eng-runtime to coordinate patches. good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
